pairs.subject: agent-memory
pairs.evidence: app/api/companion/[id]/message/route.ts:76 The route reads only the newest 40 turns and passes no count of what it left out; the 12-turn window is cut again downstream, and companion_cli.py:339 shows the result to the model as 'THIS CONVERSATION SO FAR'. In a long thread the model never learns that older turns are stored but not shown.

techniques.evidence: app/api/companion/[id]/message/route.ts:76 Window-of-newest site with no in-band notice of kind/count/cause. Downstream transcriptWindow (12) and _render_transcript also cut silently, under a header that implies completeness.

app/api/companion/threads/route.ts:47 The dock boot payload says whether memory is on, so 'memory off' and 'remembered nothing' read differently. This only covers the consent-off case; a failed brain read is not shown in this context.

app/api/companion/brain/route.ts:17 A human consent gate sits before any memory creation, adoption or write. The birth step never overwrites a constitution or identity the operator already wrote (line 26).

app/api/companion/[id]/message/route.ts:35 Capture happens at each exchange and the user turn is stored before the model call, so a provider failure loses the reply but never the question. The stored turn's meta also points to the episodes the brain wrote (line 139).

declined.subject: agent-memory
declined.reason: The context holds no agent memory: its 'governance cache' (governanceCacheSync.ts) serves a stored group-evaluation result, and recall, episode and belief do not appear in app/features/hiring/decisions. But 'consolidat' and 'memory' do appear in sibling files there (selection-memory-rerun, a UI consolidation note), and the re-run search covers that directory, so I could not choose absence terms safely. Declined instead of risking a refused not-applicable verdict.
